JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellants/petitioners challenging the judgment and award passed by the Court of the Member, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapura (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.613/2018 dated 17.12.2021, on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are;
The petitioners are the parents of the deceased Prabhu S/o Basappa Chabanur @ Madar.

That on 22.05.2018 at about 7.45 hours the deceased was sitting on the parked motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-28/EK-4565 near the land of one Ningayya Bachyal on Hirur-Sasanur road, at that time the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-28/TB-3866 came in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, being driven by its driver dashed against the motor cycle on which the deceased was sitting,
as a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same on the spot.
4. It is stated that the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years.
He was doing agricultural work and thereby earning monthly income of `15,000/-.
The deceased was the only earning member of the family, who used to look after the petitioners and the family was depending on his income.
In view of the sudden and untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their sole bread earner, love and affection and also have suffered mentally and financially.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

5. On service of notice, respondent No.1 placed exparte, however respondent No.2 filed detailed statement of objections denying inter alia age, avocation and income including the death of deceased as alleged in the claim petition.

It is further pleaded that the tractor was duly insured and the policy was inforce and the driver of the tractor was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident and that the terms and conditions of the policy has been violated.
It is further pleaded that the accident was because of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, on the basis of this, sought for dismissal of claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the father of the deceased examined as PW.1 and Basappa S/O Hulageppa Chabanur @ Madar ... vs Siddanna And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25657520/

sentences.text: 2 one independent witness examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P9.

Respondents have not examined any of the witnesses but with consent got marked Ex.R1, the insurance policy of the tractor.
7.

On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the Tribunal fastened liability on the respondents and awarded total compensation of `13,54,000/- with 6% interest per annum and directed the respondent No.2/Insurance Company to deposit the compensation.

8. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous, contrary to the material evidence placed on record and the documents presented by the petitioners.
On this basis, they seek enhancement of compensation and consequently allow the appeal.

9. Per contra, learned counsel Sri Manvendra Reddy, appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 vehemently contends that, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in consonance with the material evidence placed on record and the same in fact is on the higher side.

Learned counsel further contends that the award of compensation on the other heads are suitably calculated and rightly awarded, which does not call for interference and on the basis of these submissions, he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioners.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the petitioners are entitled to enhancement of compensation ?
ii) What order"
11.

On a careful perusal of entire material on record and having gone through the impugned judgment and award including the exhibits marked in the case on hand, it is apparently seen that the petitioners would be entitled for enhancement of compensation for the reason stated herein below :-
a.
It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 22.05.2018 at 7.45 a.m. between tractor and motorcycle leading to the death of deceased-Prabhu S/o Basappa Chabanur @ Madar.
These aspects have been proved by way of production of Ex.P1 to P7, which are police records.
Admittedly, there is no challenge made to the initiation of criminal prosecution and laying of charge-sheet.
The Insurance Company has not filed any appeal against the judgment and award.

Under the circumstances, there is no requirement for this Court to delve into the occurrence of accident, involvement of the vehicles and so also the death having occurred due to the road traffic accident.

sentences.text: Now, the question that is to be decided by this Court is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and whether calls for interference by this Court.

It is relevant to quote the decision in Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court noticed that Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act enjoins the claims Tribunal to make an award determining "the amount of compensation which appears to be just".

entities.text: Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the objective factors,
which may constitute the basis of (2009) 2 SCC 225 compensation appearing as just, have not been indicated in the Act.

Thus, the expression "which appears to be just"
vests wide discretion in the Claims Tribunal in the matter of determination of compensation.

Nevertheless, the wide amplitude of such power does not empower the Tribunal to determine the compensation arbitrarily or to ignore settled principles relating to the determination of the compensation.

Similarly, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to the persons liable to pay compensation.

c. The determination of the compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependents of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the petitioners has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.

The determination of the quantum must answer what "contemporary society would deem to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrong doer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing".
The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the "law values life and limb in a free Society in generous case".
At the same time, misplaced sympathy, generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining compensation.

The object of providing compensation is to please the petitioners to the extent possible, in almost the same financial position as they were in before the accident and not to make a fortune out of misfortune that has befallen them.

d. On the basis of the material evidence placed before this Court, it is seen that the deceased was aged about 24 years and doing agricultural work and earning `15,000/-
per month.
The Tribunal has rightly taken the monthly income of the deceased at `11,750/- and same is taken.

The deceased being aged 24 years is entitled to 40%
towards future prospects in addition to the notional income chart value for assessment of income.
In view of the fact that the deceased was aged 24 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '18' which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.
Same does not call for interference.

e. Evidently, the deceased Prabhu was doing agricultural work, addition of 40%
towards loss of future prospects to be added as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, which would be `16,450/- (`11,750/- + 4,700 (40%)).

The annual income would be `98,700/- (8,225x12).

g.

Petitioner No.1 being the father who died and legal representation is brought on record i.e.,
petitioner No.2.
Petitioner No.2 being the mother of the deceased has lost her beloved son being bread earner.

Since there are two dependants they being the parents, but in the present case the father of the deceased died, the dependent will be one in number i.e., mother of the deceased is entitled to `40,000/- as contemplated in the case of Pranay Sethi stated supra, which has been subsequently followed in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others5.

Towards 'loss of estate' and towards 'transportation of dead body & funeral expenses', petitioners would be entitled to `15,000/- each i.e., a sum of `30,000/- requires to be awarded and it is accordingly awarded.
Accordingly, under conventional head `70,000/- (loss of consortium `40,000/- + loss of estate `15,000/- + Towards transportation of dead body & funeral expenses `15,000/-) is awarded.
i. As per the decision in Pranay Sethi, stated supra, 10% on the conventional head for each block period requires to be awarded, which in the present case would be `7,000/- for one block period.

Thus the appellant/petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation as under:
